prize_parts.citation: For discoveries in the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the incretin effect, and for their translation into long-acting incretin therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: All six of us put GLP-1 first, and I still think that is right on the merits and not just because of the vote count. It is a complete arc from hormone physiology (the incretin effect, proglucagon processing, GLP-1 and GLP-2 biology) through the problem of rapid degradation to long-acting agonists with large independent outcome trials in diabetes, obesity, and cardiovascular and renal disease. The physiology and the drug design are both necessary parts of the chain, so a trio of Holst and Drucker for the physiology and Knudsen for the drug design describes the achievement faithfully and fits within three names.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is credit. Mojsov's identification of the biologically active GLP-1(7-36) form is a real contribution that three of my colleagues name, and Habener is not even on the supplied list. A prize that omits both can look like it rewards industrial development over discovery. There is also a risk of lumping basic physiology and pharmaceutical engineering into one citation without making the intellectual contribution of each clear.

responses.point: Sandberg proposes Drucker, Holst and Mojsov for B041, treating Knudsen as a fourth name, and also puts B007 (SMN2 antisense) third.
responses.response: I take the Mojsov point seriously and cannot dismiss it. But the prize is for the achievement, and without the step to long-acting analogues the discovery would not have reached patients at the scale that makes it prize-worthy. Knudsen's work on acylation and half-life extension was a creative solution, not routine development, so I would keep her ahead of Mojsov, while accepting that this is a judgement call on which we may differ. On B007 I agree it is a clean mechanism-to-drug story, but I rank it below CAR-T and optogenetics because the disease is rare and the antisense platform's broader reach is still being shown.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius ranks B004 (BCR-ABL inhibition) second, citing clean credit and more than twenty years of survival data, and B022 (anti-TNF) third.
responses.response: I agree that credit in B004 is cleaner than in most candidates, and the maturity argument is strong. My reservation is that imatinib is the template for kinase-inhibitor oncology, while CAR-T opened a new therapeutic modality, which I think is the larger conceptual step. I do not regard that as decisive, and if the committee wants a clean three-person prize with no attribution dispute, B004 is a serious alternative to the CAR-T group, whose credit also leaves out Eshhar. I would like to hear why you place it above B035.

responses.point: Linnarsson ranks B034 (HPV VLP vaccines) third, above optogenetics, citing a rare molecular discovery that prevents cancer at population scale.
responses.response: The effectiveness data are persuasive, and I agree the Lowy, Schiller and Frazer trio is coherent. I place B034 below B033 because of the Zhou question and because the vaccines were developed in parallel by two groups with commercial development, so the credit boundary is less clear to me than it first appears. This is a modest disagreement, and I would not oppose B034 if the committee prefers a prevention-focused prize.

responses.point: Svenningsson ranks CAR-T second and optogenetics third, and notes that any three-person split of B033 leaves out significant contributors.
responses.response: I agree on the order of B035 and B033 and share the concern about B033: six credited names for three places makes any choice contestable, and I find Bamberg's and Boyden's claims hard to set aside. This is the reason I do not push optogenetics as a first choice even though it is close to my own field. Its case rests on a research tool, and clinical translation is only beginning.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov should replace or join Knudsen cannot be settled from the supplied text, and the committee must decide how much weight to give peptide identification against analogue design.
Whether basic physiology and pharmaceutical development belong in one citation or are better described as two linked parts.
Whether the credited list for B035 is complete enough without Eshhar, and whether B004 is cleaner than B035 on attribution.
I am relying on recollection of the literature and have not verified details against primary sources.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for the shortlisted candidates. I co-authored a 2009 paper with committee colleague Thomas Perlmann and a 2019 synthesis with Sten Grillner, but neither relates to the shortlisted discoveries. Optogenetics (B033) is in my general field, but I have no documented involvement with its credited names.
